races.name: Dunbrody Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Impero
runners_data.note: Has solid recent form including a runner-up at this course over 17f on Good, and Cian Collins' stable is in a quiet patch (0/5 in 14 days); races naturally up with the pace but the field density means he is unlikely to achieve his usual forward berth, which blunts his effectiveness here.|
runners_data.comment: A useful hurdler who shaped with considerable promise on his fencing debut, travelling powerfully before tiring close home; back at two miles, where he is most effective, he tops our ratings by a clear margin and has more to offer as his chasing career develops.

runners_data.name: Nadia's Boy
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained six-year-old who has won two of his last three starts including over 18f and 16f on Good, giving him strong course-condition profile; Brian Hayes rides but with 61 days off and a field full of prominent runners, he will struggle to find his customary forward position and that gap in race fitness is a real question.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins from his last four starts, including on the point circuit, underline genuine potential over fences; his latest outing appeared to come too soon and the trip may not be ideal long-term, but he is a clear threat on his best form.

runners_data.name: Scalpnagoon
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends him out with Jack Kennedy aboard — always a combination to respect — and he has a consistent placed record on Good ground including a second over 17f; wears tongue-tie, is a genuine prominent racer who should secure a decent pitch, but has not won in his last five starts and may just lack the finishing kick to overhaul a front-runner dictating his own terms.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Roscommon last time on softer going than he prefers, where he was ridden too prominently; he handles the trip and is at his best on decent ground, first-time tongue-tie is added, and while a handicap context may suit better in time, he could still be a threat.

runners_data.name: Soir De Garde
runners_data.note: Mullins eight-year-old with a win over 16f on Good to his name and consistent placed efforts; 62 days off is the main query but Sean O'Keeffe is an accomplished handler of a waiting hold in this situation, and his profile makes him the most natural rival to William Tell if he can slot in second early.|
runners_data.comment: His jumping completely broke down when pulled up at Punchestown last time, accounting for two non-completions in recent starts; he looked a smart prospect earlier in his hurdles career and handles today's trip and going, with his trainer firing well and giving him every chance to respond.

runners_data.name: Wendrock
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator — the only true closer in the field — but his recent form is deeply concerning: a pulled-up run, a twentieth-place finish on Soft, and only one win from 14 runs on any going; wears a hood and faces the structural disadvantage of needing a strong pace that William Tell has no reason to supply.|
runners_data.comment: Out of form and beaten a very long way at Punchestown last time, where he was sent too far ahead on his chase debut and failed to last home; he handles the trip and acts with cut in the ground, and first-time cheekpieces may help him settle better.

runners_data.name: William Tell
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, who has won twice in recent starts and shaped well over 18f on Good; Cian Quirke takes the ride for a small yard (0/1 in 14 days) and William Tell faces questions beyond 2m having been keener over shorter, but the uncontested lead on Good ground is a powerful tactical advantage in a beginners' chase.|
runners_data.comment: He became overexcited up in trip at Punchestown last time and failed to see it out; first-time tongue-tie is fitted and two miles looks more suitable, but he has something to prove on his switch to fences despite wins on his recent record.

races.paceDynamic: William Tell is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, he should stride into an uncontested position from the outset and control tempo on his own terms over this 2m trip on Good ground. Soir De Garde is mapped as a prominent racer and looks most likely to track William Tell in second, while Scalpnagoon, Impero and Nadia's Boy are all natural prominent types who cannot all occupy their preferred position — Scalpnagoon (Jack Kennedy, Gordon Elliott) and Soir De Garde (Sean O'Keeffe, Mullins) are best placed to actually secure a forward berth given their handlers' tactical clout, with Impero and Nadia's Boy likely pushed further back than ideal. Wendrock is a genuine hold-up horse and will race last or near last from the outset. With William Tell able to dictate a sustainable, unforced gallop and likely only one horse able to track him closely, this race shape strongly favours either the front-runner who controls throughout or a prominently ridden horse with a clean trip — genuine closers are structurally disadvantaged because the only true hold-up runner (Wendrock) has patchy recent form and the redistributed prominent types will not be in their ideal position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: William Tell Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If William Tell is allowed to stride clear and control a measured pace without any genuine challenger sitting on his shoulder.
scenarios.body: If William Tell is allowed to stride clear and control a measured pace without any genuine challenger sitting on his shoulder.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If William Tell is tracked closely enough by Soir De Garde or Scalpnagoon that they have enough energy conserved to overhaul him at the last fence or on the run-in.
scenarios.body: If William Tell is tracked closely enough by Soir De Garde or Scalpnagoon that they have enough energy conserved to overhaul him at the last fence or on the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Congestion Disrupts Pace Order
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of natural prominent types causes crowding early, forcing William Tell to go faster or resulting in jumping errors that scramble the race.
scenarios.body: If the cluster of natural prominent types causes crowding early, forcing William Tell to go faster or resulting in jumping errors that scramble the race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce from Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final circuit or jumping errors remove the leaders, allowing Wendrock or a hold-up Impero to finish through.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the final circuit or jumping errors remove the leaders, allowing Wendrock or a hold-up Impero to finish through.

watchPoints.text: William Tell's jumping under pressure — any early fence error could allow Soir De Garde or Scalpnagoon to seize the lead and fundamentally alter the race shape.

Watch for early crowding as Scalpnagoon, Soir De Garde, Nadia's Boy and Impero all want to race prominently — a messy first fence could force William Tell to quicken sharply, compromising his stamina over 2m.
Nadia's Boy's 61-day absence is notable for a horse who needs a forward position he is unlikely to get — if he is race-rusty and back in the pack, Brian Hayes will have very little race to run.|

Wendrock (hood) is the only genuine hold-up horse and will tell us whether the pace is truly honest — if he is making ground from the back of the final bend, the front-runners are tiring and the race is more open than the shape suggests.

Gordon Elliott's two runners (Scalpnagoon, Wendrock) at the same meeting with Jack Kennedy and Danny Gilligan respectively — if Elliott has a stable preference it may be telegraphed by how Scalpnagoon is ridden early.

races.name: Tintern Trails Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: An Peann Dearg
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Paul Nolan who has failed to beat seven horses in four of his last five; 54 days since last run is a slight freshness query, tongue tie worn, and a 2m chase on Good suits in theory, but this race shape — compressed and pace-controlled — offers little for a confirmed closer to attack.|
runners_data.comment: His jumping let him down when pulled up at this track last time; first-time tongue-tie is the main addition, and while he handles today's trip and going, he has lacked consistency in recent starts and our figures rank him near the foot of the field.

runners_data.name: Trasna Na Pairce
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and architect of the race shape; Henry De Bromhead's charge has a solid Good-ground record (11/13) but a STYLE_FIT flag highlights she is operating outside her most comfortable role — winning from the front in a handicap chase demands jumping accuracy throughout, and her form figures of 420-52 suggest she places rather than wins when asked to dictate.|
runners_data.comment: Second at Kilbeggan on his most recent start, he shaped well enough stepped up in trip; first-time cheekpieces are fitted and his trainer is in sharp current form, though he remains yet to win in recent outings and needs to improve to feature.

runners_data.name: Ma Belle Etoile
runners_data.note: Fascinating entry for De Bromhead returning from 320 days off — two wins at 16f on Good ground are directly relevant, and a prominent style means she slots naturally into the race shape; the long absence is the only credible concern in what looks a straightforward tactical scenario for her profile.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her recent starts confirm she handles today's trip and conditions well; she was comfortably held on her latest outing, and the official mark she carries could prove testing, but her recent winning profile makes her a genuine contender.

runners_data.name: Mercury Mission
runners_data.note: Consistently prominent and consistent on Good ground (10/15 sim-going), Liam McKenna claiming 3lb is a plus at this level; three second-place finishes at 2m on Good make this trip and conditions ideal, and he should be travelling well off Trasna's fractions.|
runners_data.comment: A consistent performer in recent starts who was beaten just three lengths at Tramore last time, he has the profile to go close here; first-time cheekpieces are added, he handles today's trip and conditions, and our figures rate him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Solsbury Hill
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by Conor O'Dwyer returning after 186 days — tongue tie worn, won at 16f on Good before, but a patchy recent record (41790-) and a long break against a moderate-paced 2m chase make it hard to see where the winning move comes from structurally.|
runners_data.comment: Back from a lengthy absence, he won on his chase debut but that success may have been flattered by the nature of the race; he was well held at Leopardstown since, and first-time tongue-tie is the change here, though our figures rank him at the foot of the field.

runners_data.name: Femme Magnifique
runners_data.note: Won last time at 16f on Good for David Harry Kelly, which fits the conditions squarely; a prominent style means she is naturally positioned to exploit this steady pace, and Cian Quirke should be able to slot her in a perfect pitch just off the pace setter.|
runners_data.comment: A mare who landed a handicap at Tramore last time by over four lengths on a reduced mark, she handles today's trip and going well; her debut profile suggests she retains more to give at this level, keeping her firmly in the mix.

runners_data.name: Jane Eire
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's third runner is a genuine hold-up type (hg:ht) whose last five runs are all mid-to-rear finishing positions; Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim helps, but six-from-the-back finishes over 20f trips don't inspire confidence in a sharp 2m contest where the pace is unlikely to set the race up for closers.|
runners_data.comment: Our figures give her a clear chance in this field, and she handles today's trip and conditions; first-time hood and tongue-tie are fitted, the trainer is in good form, and she can be expected to improve on what looked like a comeback run last time.

runners_data.name: Be Fierce
runners_data.note: Prominent-style chaser with a patchy record (910-44 in recent form) for T M Walsh; won at 16f on Heavy/Good at Hea, but two consecutive fourths and a going preference leaning soft are minor concerns — Gavin Brouder rides and should get a position close enough if the horse travels.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Punchestown last time in a contest dominated from the front, where he had too much ground to make up; he handles today's trip and going, first-time tongue-tie is applied, and there is a solid case for him performing better here.

runners_data.name: Party President
runners_data.note: Showed a second last time at 16f on Soft for Dylan O'Connor (7lb claim); genuinely a hold-up type and his sim-going record on Good is only 6/12, the weakest in the field — this combination of style mismatch and ground uncertainty makes him an outsider in this shape despite recent encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: A step down in class brought out a better display at Roscommon last time, where he finished second; he handles today's trip and conditions and is still finding his feet over fences, though he remains yet to score in recent outings and needs further progress to feature.

runners_data.name: Presenting Lad
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural rear-of-field positioning is already under structural pressure in this race — mapped to midfield on redistribution but unlikely to push forward in practice; ten-year-old with form figures of 7P-920 recently, and the sim-going record of 13/15 (field size, not win rate) does not flatter.|
runners_data.comment: His latest run at Roscommon came on ground that went against him, yet he shaped with more promise than the finishing position suggests; first-time tongue-tie is fitted, he favours today's trip and going, and the mark he carries looks workable if this sees an upturn.

runners_data.name: Tequila Talkin'
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer for Paul Nolan who cannot secure that berth in this crowded front-end — the STYLE_FIT discount is real, and 54 days off matches stablemate An Peann Dearg; last run of second at 16f on Good is the best recent form in the book, but his ability to reproduce that from a midfield position is the key doubt.|
runners_data.comment: Second here last time beaten just over a length, she handles both the course and today's going; first-time hood is fitted and she may benefit from a more demanding test in time, but there is enough ability on show to suggest she can make her presence felt.

runners_data.name: That's About Right
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type (hg:tp) redistributed to midfield — P J Rothwell's runner has form figures of 045P-0 and has only placed in races 18f+ on various surfaces; the 2m trip looks sharper than ideal, and Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim doesn't compensate for the style-trip mismatch.|
runners_data.comment: Out of form in recent starts and well beaten at Punchestown last time, he typically races held up and handles a trip around two and a half miles; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces are fitted, but his figures suggest he has plenty to find to get involved.

runners_data.name: Mic Drop
runners_data.note: Won last time at 18f on Good for David M O'Brien and is a natural prominent racer — redistributed to midfield because of the crowded front end, Josh Williamson (5lb) takes the ride; if he can push forward as his profile suggests, he has live claims, but the STYLE_FIT penalty is real if he cannot reclaim his natural position.|
runners_data.comment: A drop in class paid dividends at Limerick last time, where he landed a handicap by two and a half lengths off a reduced mark; he stays the trip well, though today's distance may be on the shorter side for his ideal conditions, and this is stiffer company.

races.paceDynamic: Trasna Na Pairce is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press it early, is set to control proceedings from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m. Ma Belle Etoile, Mercury Mission, and Femme Magnifique will push for prominent positions behind the leader, creating an organised early order rather than a scramble, though the pace itself is unlikely to be truly searching. This moderate, controlled tempo over a sharp 2m trip on a flat track will compress the field and compress finishing windows, rewarding horses that travel prominently with cover and can produce a clean, decisive jump at the final fence rather than those grinding from the rear. Prominent racers and close-tracking types hold a clear structural advantage here — hold-up horses will find it difficult to manufacture enough momentum from off the pace when the gallop is steady. Several runners — Tequila Talkin', Mic Drop, and Presenting Lad — are genuine prominent or hold-up types who have been redistributed on the map because they cannot all hold their natural position in this field; of these, Mic Drop and Tequila Talkin' are most likely to push forward and attempt to reclaim a prominent berth, while Presenting Lad is the truest hold-up horse and the least likely to do so.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trasna Dictates, Closers Shut Out
scenarios.trigger: If Trasna Na Pairce bowls along comfortably in front, setting a routine Good-ground pace that nobody seriously challenges.
scenarios.body: If Trasna Na Pairce bowls along comfortably in front, setting a routine Good-ground pace that nobody seriously challenges.
winners: Trasna Na Pairce sets it up for herself or Ma Belle Etoile to pick her off late
while Mercury Mission and Femme Magnifique are best placed to capitalise from a prominent pitch.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types push for position early and the tempo picks up through the back straight, fragmenting the field.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent types push for position early and the tempo picks up through the back straight, fragmenting the field.
winners: both proven on Good ground at this trip
are ideally profiled to pounce in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace causes a bunching effect that produces a sprint finish and hold-up horses find a clear run from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the steady pace causes a bunching effect that produces a sprint finish and hold-up horses find a clear run from the rear.
winners: An Peann Dearg has course-and-distance form but is compromised by a hold-up style in a race that won't truly set it up; Party President showed a close second last time but relies on a truly muddling pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Movers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If trainer Henry De Bromhead's trio (Trasna Na Pairce, Ma Belle Etoile, Jane Eire) operate as a de-facto team and the stable's tactical positioning proves decisive.
scenarios.body: If trainer Henry De Bromhead's trio (Trasna Na Pairce, Ma Belle Etoile, Jane Eire) operate as a de-facto team and the stable's tactical positioning proves decisive.
winners: returning from 320 days off but with two wins on Good ground at exactly this trip
could outclass a modest handicap field if freshness translates to sharpness; Mic Drop
a winner last time at 18f on Good
would be the chief danger as a redistributed prominent type who battles forward.

watchPoints.text: Ma Belle Etoile returns from 320 days off with two course-trip wins on Good — watch if she jumps cleanly first two fences as a sign that the layoff hasn't blunted her sharpness, which would make her the dominant presence in this shape.

Mercury Mission is 3W6P on similar going and shapes as the most consistent horse in the race; watch his position rounding the home turn — if he is within two lengths of Trasna Na Pairce at that point, he is very hard to keep out.

Mic Drop and Tequila Talkin' will both attempt to push forward from their mapped midfield positions — watch the first three fences to see if either forces their way into a prominent berth, as doing so would change their probability profile significantly.

Trasna Na Pairce's jumping under early pressure is the key watch point — if she is rushed or makes an error at the first open ditch, the pace dynamic collapses and the race becomes far more open for hold-up horses.

Femme Magnifique's last-to-first win at 16f on Good last time makes her a horse to monitor through the middle mile — if she travels smoothly in third or fourth, the compressed tempo of this race is tailor-made for her late kick off a sound jumping round.

races.name: Duncannon Beach Handicap Chase (0-100)

runners_data.name: Shannon Bank
runners_data.note: Recent winner (1st last time, 29 days ago) making him the highest-rated front-runner at OR 100; Sean O'Keeffe retains the ride for a trainer with a cold strike-rate (0/5 T14), but the horse's natural pace-forcing style suits this 2m trip on Good ground perfectly and he is the one to beat in shape.
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap hurdle at Listowel 29 days ago by three parts of a length after a drop in grade, and she is still progressing in this sphere; effective at 2–2½m on today's going and largely unexposed over fences, she is a strong danger to the selection.

runners_data.name: Figurehead
runners_data.note: Consistent on Good going (8/15 similar-going runs) but this nine-year-old's hold-up style is his natural mode, and with Simon Torrens aboard he will need the pace to truly stack up to get competitive from the back; the headgear (tongue-tie) suggests connections are chasing a return to form after a run of poor finishes including a P and a 13th.
runners_data.comment: Beaten at Punchestown 48 days ago in what shaped as a fitness run, he is expected to strip sharper; acts on today's going and his performances over fences have been more convincing, making him a genuine danger despite being yet to score in his last five starts. First-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Miss Oreo
runners_data.note: Josh Williamson (5lb claim) partners this mare for John Joseph Hanlon who is 0/5 in the T14 window; her natural hold-up style has yielded only two placed efforts in 15 similar-going runs and a recent sequence of 9,0,4,0,P offers little encouragement for a race this competitive.
runners_data.comment: Bled at Killarney 50 days ago and was pulled up; back after a break and effective at around 2½m, but form has been well below expectations all term and the going could be on the sharp side for her, making it hard to make a case. First-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Tumuch
runners_data.note: Returning from 93 days off (65-day P noted) and while Tom Dreaper's runner won at 2m on Good going, the lengthy absence and predominantly hold-up style mean he arrives needing things to fall just right; his tongue-tie and modest recent form on Good ground (5/8 runs) add to the risk.
runners_data.comment: Won a novice at Fairyhouse by twenty lengths last time and has multiple wins from points, but has yet to make that form tell over fences under Rules and this competitive handicap looks a stiff enough test; effective at 2½–3m, with first-time tongue-tie applied.

runners_data.name: Jouster
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's seven-year-old has placed three times in 15 similar-going runs including a win, and Danny Gilligan keeps the ride; naturally a hold-up horse, his recent form string (4,3,4) shows consistent proximity to the frame and the 2m trip on Good looks fine, making him a realistic each-way proposition if the pace plays out strongly.
runners_data.comment: Promised a little more in the two preceding runs but was well beaten at Roscommon 22 days ago; handles 2½m with cut in the ground and the dual headgear change is a notable switch, but he is yet to score in his last five starts. First-time tongue-tie and blinkers.

runners_data.name: Auntie Lacey
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's mare has sound course form (7/7 similar-going runs, placed once) and is ridden by 5lb claimer Alan O'Sullivan; her natural hold-up style means she is genuinely at a disadvantage in a race dominated by pace-setters, and the 0W record in similar conditions tempers enthusiasm even at OR 92.
runners_data.comment: Beaten ten lengths at Downpatrick 39 days ago when the trip looked shorter than ideal; she shaped well enough to suggest more is coming as the distances increase, acts on today's going, and is a genuine danger despite being winless in her last five starts. First-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Quinn The Eskimo
runners_data.note: Carl Millar (5lb) takes the mount for Nolan's other runner, and this six-year-old has won once on Good going; however, he is a genuine closer now shunted into a midfield map position by an overcrowded hold-up division, and his recent form of 7,7,P,4 on similar ground suggests he is not firing consistently enough to overcome positional disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Limerick 40 days ago without clear mitigation; his earlier career form was promising but he has not built on it and his record in recent starts is short on encouragement. Effective at 2–2¼m on today's going, but yet to score. First-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue rides the most form-consistent closer in the race — OR 92, won 16 days ago, placed five times in 14 similar-going runs — and this horse's back-to-basics profile of winning on Good at 18f makes him the most credible hold-up challenger; the tight 16-day turnaround is the only flag.
runners_data.comment: Won by five lengths at Downpatrick three starts ago off this mark and followed up with a runner-up finish there most recently; well treated on hurdle form and largely unexplored in this sphere, she is rated top on our figures and is the one to beat. First-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Polly Poppins
runners_data.note: Bernard Crowley's six-year-old has shown a natural prominent style and the 12/13 similar-going record confirms comfort on Good ground; Michael Kenneally (5lb) claims, and recent placed efforts at this trip (2nd, 3rd) suggest genuine competitiveness if she can track the pace-setters and pounce late.
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held at Tramore 32 days ago in what appeared a fitness run; her earlier form has been backed up in places and the mark is fair, but inconsistency is a recurring concern and she is yet to score in her last five starts. Effective at 2m on today's going.

runners_data.name: L'Amiral Fromentin
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe's booking is notable for PJ Rothwell's five-year-old, but this horse is a natural hold-up type now squeezed into the midfield by race shape; a 0W record in 9 similar-going appearances and a recent form string of 9,3,6,3,0 shows inconsistency, and the pace headset (hood) has not yet produced a win at this level.
runners_data.comment: Showed fair form before Roscommon 22 days ago, where he failed to get competitive and may have found the going too testing; effective at 2–2¼m on sound ground, which applies today, and first-time cheekpieces are a positive angle, though he is yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Kingdom Calling
runners_data.note: The ⚠ fades-in-finish flag is significant for a horse whose last six runs show a pattern of mid-table finishes (6,10,P,7,9); GB Noonan rides for Eoin McCarthy (0/0 T14) and while this six-year-old has been placed once in 15 similar-going runs, his tendency to weaken late makes a strongly-run 2m particularly demanding.
runners_data.comment: Out of the picture throughout his chase debut at Tramore 32 days ago and in need of a much better effort; effective at 2m on today's going, but he has yet to score in his last five starts and a significant step forward is required. First-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Benzine
runners_data.note: Shane Fitzgerald partners this seven-year-old for J Morrison and the ⚠ fades flag combined with a 0W record in 15 similar-going starts paints a limited picture; a recent placed effort (2nd, 4th) shows he can run creditably but the finishing weakness is a real liability when two front-runners are sure to burn bright early and test every runner's stamina.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Clonmel 25 days ago despite jumping errors that cost him ground; his earlier chase debut was encouraging and he handles the distance, but the hurdles profile is exposed and he is yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Chosen Shant
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin is an eye-catching booking for Aengus King's ten-year-old, whose 2W record in 15 similar-going runs is the strongest historical win-rate among the hold-up pack; at OR 85 the weight concession to classier rivals is significant, but the pairing of an elite jockey and a horse who has genuinely made the frame (3rd, 4th) keeps him in the mix.
runners_data.comment: Well positioned at Roscommon 22 days ago but well beaten when it mattered; effective at 2m–3m and handles any going, though her best form may flatter somewhat and she has yet to score in her last five starts. First-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Ahellofaman
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon saddles this four-year-old, the youngest in the field at a featherweight 140lbs, with Gavin Brouder aboard; a 0W0P record in 10 similar-going starts is concerning, and the horse's natural hold-up profile combined with limited chase experience and a 67-day layoff leaves him facing a stiff ask on debut in this company.
runners_data.comment: Looked a factor briefly at Kilbeggan 67 days ago before fading, possibly finding the trip too long; a return to fences after a break and over a shorter distance could help, but he is yet to score in his last five starts and is hard to make a case for.

runners_data.name: Sampoet
runners_data.note: Ben Harvey rides this nine-year-old for DM Christie (0/0 T14) and Sampoet is the second confirmed front-runner in the race; a headgear (blinkers) entry underlines that connections want early energy, but a form string of F,4,5,8,4 and a 0W record in 12 similar-going runs suggests he is more likely to pressure Shannon Bank than beat him.
runners_data.comment: Finished fourth at Downpatrick 17 days ago, coping better with the step up in trip; effective at 2m4f–3m on a sound surface, which applies today, but inconsistency is a recurring issue and he is yet to score in his last five starts. First-time blinkers could help him focus.

runners_data.name: Sunwalk
runners_data.note: The ⚠ fades flag and an 85-day layoff for Seamus Neville's eight-year-old are the headline concerns; a natural hold-up horse now mapped to midfield by an overcrowded rear division, his PP2P9 recent form and 0W record in 15 similar-going runs make it hard to construct a winning scenario unless the race is uniquely tactical — which two front-runners make essentially impossible.
runners_data.comment: Off for 85 days after over-racing at Cork and fading badly; a maiden over hurdles with plenty to prove in this sphere, he has yet to score in his last five starts and is hard to fancy, though the reduced mark offers a sliver of hope.

races.paceDynamic: Shannon Bank and Sampoet are the two confirmed front-runners in a 16-horse field and both will want to lead, creating a genuinely contested pace from the off over 2m on Good ground at Wexford. Shannon Bank (OR 100, won last time out) is the classier of the two pace-setters and is likely to assert for the lead early, with Sampoet pressing and ensuring the gallop is honest rather than dawdling. The resulting race shape — an unrelenting tempo set by two genuine front-runners — will stretch the field and put a premium on jumping fluency and stamina, favouring horses that can track the pace from a prominent position without over-racing, rather than those forced wide or deep into the chasing pack. Polly Poppins and Jouster are the most natural prominent-position horses able to exploit the pace; the field carries a heavy concentration of hold-up types — Quinn The Eskimo, Auntie Lacey, L'Amiral Fromentin, Kingdom Calling, Benzine, Chosen Shant, and Ahellofaman are all genuine closers redistributed into midfield on the map because the race simply will not compress enough to give them their natural position, and Sea Of Doubt is the truest hold-up horse best placed to navigate the traffic and finish from off the pace. This race shape most strongly favours horses racing prominently just off the front two, who can pounce when the pace-setters tire at the last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Shannon Bank and Sampoet fight for the lead and set a genuinely taxing gallop that burns both out in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: If Shannon Bank and Sampoet fight for the lead and set a genuinely taxing gallop that burns both out in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Shannon Bank asserts dominance over Sampoet early, settles into a controlled rhythm, and is never seriously pressured.
scenarios.body: If Shannon Bank asserts dominance over Sampoet early, settles into a controlled rhythm, and is never seriously pressured.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to exhaust both leaders but the true hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: If the pace is strong enough to exhaust both leaders but the true hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Get Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow moderates mid-race and the field concertinas, giving genuine hold-up horses a clear run from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the pace somehow moderates mid-race and the field concertinas, giving genuine hold-up horses a clear run from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Shannon Bank and Sampoet will fight for the lead from the gates — watch whether Shannon Bank asserts cleanly or whether a sustained early duel burns both horses out before the final fence.

Sea Of Doubt is the form hold-up horse (recent winner, Keith Donoghue up) but is buried in a congested pack; watch whether Donoghue can find clear daylight turning for home or if traffic denies him a clean run.

Chosen Shant gets an elite jockey booking in JJ Slevin and, unusually among the hold-up pack, has a genuine win record on similar ground — watch for Slevin finding a position closer to the pace than his natural style would suggest.

Polly Poppins is the most naturally prominent horse outside the two leaders and the likeliest beneficiary if the front-runners exhaust each other; watch whether Michael Kenneally (5lb) can hold a close-up position without over-committing.

With seven redistributed hold-up horses all competing for midfield positions, jumping errors and interference are elevated risks at the early fences — watch the first two fences for fallers or hampered runners that could compromise several each-way contenders simultaneously.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Leave In Secret
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner here under Dylan Kidd for Thomas Gibney, who is 0/2 in the last 14 days; Good ground suits (12/15 similar-going record) and the uncontested lead is a major asset at 2m7f, though its STYLE_FIT tag as a natural prominent rather than true leader means its chance may deflate if it cannot sustain the gallop over this extended trip.
runners_data.comment: That latest effort at Downpatrick 17 days ago had the look of a fitness outing and he is expected to improve; handles today's going, effective at 2–2½m, and rates a genuine threat despite being winless in his last five starts. First-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Harbour Highway
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins runner (0/4 T14) who placed twice on Good at 20-24f and posted a win at 22f on Good — exactly the right profile for this trip and surface; sits naturally prominent and should slot in just behind Leave In Secret without burning energy.
runners_data.comment: Showed decent prior form but raced too freely at Roscommon 22 days ago and was well held; handles today's going and distance, with a win to his name in recent starts, though inconsistency makes him hard to support here. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Sammy Smart
runners_data.note: Ageing ten-year-old for Gibney who has placed twice on Good at 22-24f and is comfortable racing prominently; the recent unseating (U) is a concern but the form before it included a third at 22f on Good, making them a durable if not exciting presence.
runners_data.comment: Unseated at Punchestown 24 days ago after a promising run of form that suggested the mark could still be workable; effective at 2½–3m and handles today's going, but the mishap last time raises a question over confidence and he has yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Duty Bound
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for JP Flavin carrying 164lbs with 50 days off — the layoff is worth noting; has placed at 24f on Good and runs prominently, but the P last time and the fitness query after seven weeks temper enthusiasm despite solid similar-going figures (11/15, 2W3P).
runners_data.comment: Back after 50 days following an abortive run at Killarney where he pressed on too freely; handles today's going and effective at 2½–3m, though the handicapper appears in control of his mark and he is yet to score in recent starts. First-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Riggs
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with an 11-year-old's veteran cunning, carrying 162lbs for P Cluskey; all five recent runs have been on Good or similar, making the going profile ideal, but very modest recent form (P8 in last two) means he needs the front to fold significantly.
runners_data.comment: Well held at Kilbeggan over hurdles 15 days ago but clearly a better performer in the chasing sphere; effective at 3m on today's going and a consistent competitor over fences, he rates a fair midfield chance despite being winless in his last five starts. First-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Therellbguddaysyet
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type for Paul O'Flynn who has finished 4th-8th across recent Good-ground starts; the 31 days since last run is fine, but the form string lacks a win or close placing that would inspire confidence at this level, making them more a pace presence than a likely winner.
runners_data.comment: Overextended himself at Listowel 31 days ago by racing too freely in a hurdle; he is far more interesting over fences where he is still lightly tried and open to progress, and first-time cheekpieces could help him find a rhythm despite being winless in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Rue Taylor
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's six-year-old is a genuine prominent racer who has been pushed back to midfield on the map because the field is overloaded up front; recent Good-ground form is modest (best of 5/22f) and the STYLE_FIT discount applies — if they cannot get their natural pitch, their chance diminishes considerably.
runners_data.comment: A mare who showed more over hurdles in the past but whose form has faded in recent starts, she was comfortably held in a beginners chase at Limerick 40 days ago; effective at around 3m, and first-time tongue-tie and blinkers offer a revival angle, though recent starts are short on encouragement.

runners_data.name: Teenage Kiss
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 24f on Good — the most relevant recent form in the race; naturally races prominently but the crowded front end means Conor O'Dwyer's runner may have to settle further back than ideal, though a horse with this recency of form and a proven 24f win on Good is dangerous if they do find a position.
runners_data.comment: A winner here 45 days ago by two and a half lengths, she has taken well to staying trips and steps into chasing with more to offer; effective at 2m3f–3m on today's going and rated top on our figures, she is the one to beat. First-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Secrecies Of Stone
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's eight-year-old wears a hood and has placed at 26f on Good, but recent form shows a P and a fourth — the natural prominent style has been displaced to midfield given the congestion ahead, and the FP running in the last few starts before that fourth is a concern about jumping reliability.
runners_data.comment: Unable to see out the trip at Punchestown 24 days ago; his form has been well below expectations all season and stamina over this distance is an open question. Hard to fancy, though first-time blinkers give him something fresh to work with.

runners_data.name: Menas Miracle
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 22f on Good for Brendan Oliver Walsh, which is the best piece of form credentials among the displaced prominent types; naturally wants to race handy but finds the field too congested, meaning Josh Williamson must decide early whether to fight for position or accept a midfield role that may not suit.
runners_data.comment: Won at Tramore 31 days ago, taking a handicap by three and a quarter lengths after stepping up in trip, and there is a sense she has more to offer over fences as the distances lengthen; effective at 2–2¾m and carries first-time tongue-tie, but now competing off a higher mark.

runners_data.name: Bohemian Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up type flagged as a fader in the finish — the 0/6 win-or-place record on similar going and a form string of 8850-0 tells its own story; the 45-day break does nothing to help, and this looks a horse that will struggle to reach the leaders over 2m7f.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at this venue 45 days ago where the ground could have been too quick; effective at 2½m and carrying a light weight, but consistent form has been absent and he has yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Malton Groove
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who ran second over 24f on Good most recently — the best placed of the genuine hold-up runners on form; Patrick O'Brien's claim could save vital weight, and the 17-day turnaround is fine, but the 0W3P similar-going record shows a horse that gets close without winning.
runners_data.comment: Back to something approaching his best at Downpatrick 17 days ago, beaten only half a length off a much-reduced mark; effective at 2½–3m on today's going and rated second on our figures, he is a genuine danger despite his inconsistent record as a maiden. First-time tongue-tie.

races.paceDynamic: Leave In Secret is the confirmed lone pace-setter and will dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop over 2m7f on Good ground, with no genuine rival likely to pressurise them early. The field is heavily loaded with prominent types — Harbour Highway, Sammy Smart, Duty Bound, and Therellbguddaysyet will fill the immediate chasing positions behind the leader, creating a compact early order. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Teenage Kiss, Rue Taylor, Secrecies Of Stone, and Menas Miracle are all genuine prominent racers redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning several will either have to race against their style or expend energy fighting for position in the early stages. With a lone leader setting a controlled tempo over an extended trip, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types with proven stamina who can travel efficiently without burning energy early and deliver a sustained challenge from the home turn — runners currently mapped to midfield through redistribution, if they do settle, may also benefit from an uncontested pace that keeps things honest rather than gruelling.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Leave In Secret sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the chasing pack cannot close the gap entering the home straight.
scenarios.body: If Leave In Secret sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the chasing pack cannot close the gap entering the home straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chasers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Leave In Secret's advantage is eroded from the third-last as the compact chasing group applies collective pressure.
scenarios.body: If Leave In Secret's advantage is eroded from the third-last as the compact chasing group applies collective pressure.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If one of the true prominent horses mapped to midfield settles better than expected and arrives with a fresh sprint late.
scenarios.body: If one of the true prominent horses mapped to midfield settles better than expected and arrives with a fresh sprint late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race causing a dramatic slowdown that brings the rear of the field into play.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses mid-race causing a dramatic slowdown that brings the rear of the field into play.

watchPoints.text: Teenage Kiss holds the standout piece of recent form — a win over 24f on Good — and if Charlie O'Dwyer can find a position closer to the pace than the map suggests, this runner becomes the most dangerous horse in the race.

The cluster of natural prominent horses (Rue Taylor, Teenage Kiss, Secrecies Of Stone, Menas Miracle) all wanting to race up with the pace behind Leave In Secret creates significant risk of early crowding and bumping on the run to the first fence — watch for trouble in running in the opening stages.

Duty Bound's 50-day absence is the longest in the field — monitor market moves and any pre-race jockey reports, as the layoff combined with a P last time raises fitness questions that could see them fade rather than finish from a prominent position.

Harbour Highway's record of two seconds at 20-24f on Good is solid but the 0/4 T14 for Emmet Mullins is worth noting — trainer form in the immediate window is cold, and if Leave In Secret sets a true lone-leader scenario, Harbour Highway's prominent placing may not be enough to peg them back.

Riggs is the only truly confirmed hold-up runner with an unblemished Good-ground profile (15/15 runs on similar) — if the pace collapses at the home turn rather than staying honest, this veteran could emerge from the back at a price worth watching.

races.name: Cottage Autism Network Mares Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Aruntothequeen
runners_data.note: Won off this mark at Goodwood equivalent last month and has solid good-ground form (9/13 sim-going record), but genuinely wants to race prominently — crowded out of that position here by the volume of similar types, so her chance is conditional on scraping a forward berth she may not get.
runners_data.comment: Third at Limerick 33 days ago on a step up in trip, but she overdid things early and the 19-length gap reflected it. A reasonable hurdles maiden who may settle better over the longer distances on fences; effective from 2m to 2m4f on a sound surface, first-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Beauforts Storm
runners_data.note: Placed at Wexford in a 16f good-ground chase last time, giving her a course-proven angle, and her hold-up style is genuinely natural here rather than enforced, though she has not won in 15 attempts and consistency is the obvious concern.
runners_data.comment: Back down in trip at Tramore last month showed a marked upturn in form — second beaten just half a length in a beginners chase — and her hurdle record points to more ability in reserve. Effective at 2m on soft or good; bottom-rated on our figures but this was an encouraging run.

runners_data.name: Colleen Danu
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on good ground last time out which is directly relevant form, and Simon Torrens knows this mare well; she wants to race up with the pace and the sheer volume of prominent types means she'll need to be assertive from the start to claim her preferred position.
runners_data.comment: Won a handicap hurdle at Clonmel by 3½ lengths last time on favoured ground at a track where she clearly thrives, showing her best form when conditions suit. Inconsistent in general but capable on her day; first-time tongue-tie for her chase debut, where a bit more is needed.

runners_data.name: Farfromnowhere
runners_data.note: 108-day absence is the key flag here, and Paul Nolan has returned runners from layoffs without a warm-up before, but her best form is on soft ground and the good surface today may blunt her finishing effort; she is a natural prominent racer who is likely to find herself back further than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Hurdle outing at Cheltenham over three months ago was a below-par handicap debut — well beaten — but the view is that chasing may bring out the best in her and the hurdle mark was stiff. Effective at 2m4f with cut in the ground; top-rated here and a fresh start over fences makes sense.

runners_data.name: Future Prospect
runners_data.note: Trained by Willie Mullins with Brian Hayes aboard — both angles demand respect — but her recent form shows a fall and a pulled-up alongside her wins, and she is 0W in 11 Mullins runners over the last 14 days; her front-running instincts will be heavily compromised by the number of similar types in this field.
runners_data.comment: Exit from a beginners chase at Tramore last month is no reflection of her ability — she was travelling powerfully and looking the likeliest winner at the time. Top-level hurdle form in her locker and there is every reason to expect a different outcome over fences; first-time hood applies.

runners_data.name: Lady Bluebird
runners_data.note: The most tractable profile in the race, content to race off the pace, and her two wins have both come on good ground at 19-21f which fits today perfectly; Hugh Paul Finegan's string is quiet but Lady Bluebird's form profile is arguably the cleanest fit for this pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Third at Ballinrobe 35 days ago, 11 lengths back but ridden more patiently for a positive response, suggesting she is back to form. Well placed on maiden efforts for the long term, effective around 2½m on decent ground; the switch to fences is an open question but the form is live.

runners_data.name: Pampar Lady
runners_data.note: Two wins in her last five starts and a strong 13/15 record on similar going, making her the best ground-fit runner in the field; Keith Donoghue is a polished chase jockey and if she can force her way to a handy position from the off she has the profile to hit the frame.
runners_data.comment: Chase debut at Tramore last month brought a third-place finish, beaten 3 lengths after returning from a break — a solid introduction to fences for a mare who has been gradually improving. Effective at 2m, and a steadily progressive profile gives cause for confidence.

runners_data.name: Swing Davis
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's mare is the confirmed pace-setter but her style-fit tag is honest — she has won once from six attempts and her recent form reads PPU5, raising questions about her jumping reliability; the race hinges heavily on her ability to get round cleanly, which she cannot be trusted to do on this evidence.
runners_data.comment: Left behind by the pace at Listowel last month in a mares' hurdle, a run that served as a confidence-builder over today's conditions. Effective at 2m with scope for longer trips, and first-time blinkers may sharpen her up; she has the ability to be competitive here.

races.paceDynamic: Swing Davis is the one confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead from the off, she should be able to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable gallop over 2m3½f on good ground at Wexford. The field is unusually congested with prominent-style mares — Future Prospect, Farfromnowhere, Colleen Danu, Aruntothequeen and Pampar Lady all want to race handy — meaning the majority will be shuffled wider and deeper than their natural position, creating a bunched, competitive early-to-mid-race dynamic despite the lack of a genuine pace battle at the front. Lady Bluebird and Beauforts Storm are the only runners content to drop in and race off whatever tempo Swing Davis sets. Because the pace is uncontested and likely to be steady-to-fair rather than searching, this race shape strongly favours a horse who can hold a prominent position just off the leader and produce a clean round of jumping over the final stretch — closers will find conditions less forgiving given the controlled tempo. The field carries more genuinely prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: of those redistributed to midfield, Colleen Danu and Pampar Lady look most likely to actually secure a forward berth given their recent winning form and experienced pilots, while Future Prospect and Farfromnowhere are most at risk of being shuffled back into unnatural territory.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Swing Davis Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Swing Davis jumps cleanly and sets a comfortable gallop, dominating from the front with no serious challenge for the lead.
scenarios.body: If Swing Davis jumps cleanly and sets a comfortable gallop, dominating from the front with no serious challenge for the lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If one of the natural prominent mares secures a close tracking position and produces a slick round of jumping to reel Swing Davis in late.
scenarios.body: If one of the natural prominent mares secures a close tracking position and produces a slick round of jumping to reel Swing Davis in late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Benefit From Tactical Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Swing Davis meets a fence wrong or fades in the final half-mile after her uncontested lead proves deceptively taxing.
scenarios.body: If Swing Davis meets a fence wrong or fades in the final half-mile after her uncontested lead proves deceptively taxing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Creates Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fragments early as multiple prominent types jostle for position and the gallop becomes uneven with errors at fences disrupting the field.
scenarios.body: If the pace fragments early as multiple prominent types jostle for position and the gallop becomes uneven with errors at fences disrupting the field.

watchPoints.text: Swing Davis's jumping must be monitored from the first fence — a blunder or hesitation early would immediately dissolve her advantage and transform the race shape entirely.

The cluster of prominent types — Colleen Danu, Pampar Lady, Future Prospect, Farfromnowhere and Aruntothequeen — will be jostling for limited handy positions in the early stages; watch for traffic problems, bumping and compromised positions that reshape each mare's chance before the first circuit is complete.
Farfromnowhere returns from 109 days off without a clear prep run; watch her early jumping sharpness as a measure of readiness — a novicey or laboured start would confirm she needs the run.

Lady Bluebird's good-ground record at 19-21f is quietly strong and she is likely to get a cleaner passage than the prominent types caught in traffic; watch whether Ben Harvey gives her a searching gallop in the straight if the pace collapses.

Colleen Danu won last time over exactly this sort of trip on good ground — if Simon Torrens positions her on Swing Davis's heels in the first mile, monitor whether she travels more smoothly than the field through the middle section as an early indicator of her chance.

races.name: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Fund Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Ballyearl
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner returning after 337 days; placed record on Good ground gives confidence on the surface, and a prominent style means he should find a comfortable early berth just off Rockonliam without a fight.
runners_data.comment: Returning from nearly a year off the track, he was hampered at Galway last time and was left with far too much to make up — it counts as an unlucky effort and a fresh opportunity over fences is warranted. Acts on good ground; first-time tongue-tie applied.

runners_data.name: Drop A Threat
runners_data.note: Mullins hold-up runner with zero wins or places from nine runs on Good ground — a deeply unconvincing surface profile; finishing in the rear group and reliant on a strongly run race that this shape may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Fell out of contention at Tramore last month after going too hard in front — a significant reversal that requires explanation before trust can be restored. His pointing background hints at untapped ability over fences; first-time hood and tongue-tie applied, and he handles cut in the ground.

runners_data.name: In The Trenches
runners_data.note: Won last time out 16 days ago and clearly in form, but his natural desire to race prominently will be frustrated in this traffic-heavy field — he is a genuine front-rank type who will find himself shuffled back against his will, undermining his effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: First win at Downpatrick 16 days ago, clear by 5 lengths, and there may be more to come now he is off the mark. Consistent over both disciplines, effective at 2m to 2½m; the trainer is quiet at present but the horse arrives in good form.

runners_data.name: Jetovango
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a noted tendency to fade in the finish; 309 days off is a significant concern, and his best Good-ground form has come over shorter trips — the staying test here on a first run back looks tough.
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete at a point-to-point at Tattersalls Farm latest and improvement is required for his first run under Rules. Effective over 2m3f to 3m with first-time cheekpieces; he is the lowest-rated runner here on our assessment and needs to show considerably more.

runners_data.name: Juke Hill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott hold-up runner who has shown ability over 2m+ on Good ground (placed at 22f); his style suits a muddled-pace scenario and his second in a 22f Good-ground chase is the most relevant piece of form in the field for this trip and going combination.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14th on our figures, he was well beaten in a handicap hurdle at Punchestown 23 days ago after what was essentially an introductory run. Switching to fences with first-time blinkers, effective over 2m6f to 3m; a significant step forward is required here.

runners_data.name: Kashchei
runners_data.note: Won over 21f on Good ground on most recent start 55 days ago — current form is the key asset; a hold-up racer who produced a strong finish last time and is the most credible beneficiary if the pace scenario shifts.
runners_data.comment: Novice hurdle at Kelso last time ended in a wide-margin success, though it was aided by the early departure of a leading rival. Consistent overall, with more to come over fences; effective between 2m and 2m4f on any surface, returning from a short break with first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Malbas
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old who naturally wants to race close to the pace, but will be absorbed into midfield by the volume of prominent types ahead of him; his form figures in similar conditions are poor and his age works against him.
runners_data.comment: Form here has disappointed this term, running out of gas down the field most recently at this venue. Effective at 2m on a sound surface, and a drop in distance is the right direction; though he faces a stiff task on his chase return, the conditions at least are suitable.

runners_data.name: Ned In The Park
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win and multiple placings on Good ground; the amateur rider claim (7lb) is a potential concern in a 16-runner beginners chase, but his natural position just off the leader is ideal if he secures it cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Third at Clonmel 25 days ago after taking the field along at his own pace and perhaps going a bit too hard; there was ability on show despite the margin. Effective from 2m to 2m4f on soft or good, and the switch to fences could unlock further improvement.

runners_data.name: Paul Collins
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a sole win on Good ground over 22f — the distance form is there — but a 169-day absence and a run of five moderate efforts before that win make him hard to trust returning here.
runners_data.comment: A significant step backwards in first-time headgear at Punchestown nearly six months ago, trailing in well beaten, and a major improvement is needed on his return to fences. Effective from 2m to 2m6f on any surface; the switch back to chasing may help.

runners_data.name: Rockonliam
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone pace-setter; won on Good ground most recently 31 days ago and is trained by Henry De Bromhead alongside Ballyearl, giving the team full tactical awareness; his front-running role is uncontested and his Good-ground record (2W4P from 7 runs) underlines his suitability.
runners_data.comment: Won a handicap hurdle at Listowel last month by 3 lengths, form that underlines his hurdles credentials ahead of his chasing bow. Effective at 2½m on yielding or good ground, with a trainer in good order and a first-time tongue-tie; this is an interesting debut over fences.

runners_data.name: Silver Salute
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish and zero wins or places from six runs on Good ground — the combination of surface form and finishing style makes him a very difficult proposition in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well in a maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan 15 days ago, left behind when the pace quickened and crying out for a more demanding test. First-time cheekpieces applied; there is potential for progress over further on his switch to fences but he needs to improve considerably to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Clody Diamond
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing headgear, returning after 161 days; placed second over 2m on Good ground is the pick of her form, and a clean jumping round from a prominent early position is the route to relevance — the layoff is the key risk.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with ability at Down Royal five months ago — fourth beaten 11 lengths but perhaps not at her peak — and the form book reads better over fences for a yard that thrives at this track. Effective at around 2m4f on soft to heavy ground; first-time hood applied.

runners_data.name: Rockstown Girl
runners_data.note: Her true style is as a hold-up runner, though the density of hold-up types means she has been mapped into midfield; four consecutive placings on Good ground, including two thirds and a second, make her one of the more consistent performers in this field on the surface.
runners_data.comment: Third at Downpatrick 16 days ago — 8½ lengths back but with every chance — and she arrives here in good heart having shown form over both hurdles and fences recently. Effective at 2½m on decent ground, with a first-time tongue-tie; she remains a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Sophia Rose
runners_data.note: A natural front-rank racer whose preference will be undermined by the surplus of prominent types in this field, pushing her wider in the race than she'd like; her two second-place finishes on Good ground show she performs on the surface, but racing from out of her ideal position is a meaningful handicap.
runners_data.comment: Back to her best at Killarney last time, going down by just half a length in a handicap chase after being caught late — a run that shows she is in good form despite remaining maiden over fences. Effective at 2m4f on any surface; returning after a short break.

runners_data.name: Listentillitellyea
runners_data.note: A decade-old horse who wants to be prominent but will find the position occupied in this large field; form figures of 9-6-7 on Good ground recently suggest he is operating well below his best regardless of tactical position.
runners_data.comment: Form has fallen away in recent starts, and the latest outing at Downpatrick 17 days ago was a well-beaten effort that may have come too soon after his previous run. Handles 2m to 2m4f on soft or yielding ground, but he is a hard proposition to support at present.

runners_data.name: Burru
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground 36 days ago and has a strong Good-ground record overall (15 runs, 2W9P); a prominent racer who should be able to secure a natural position near the pace in this field and whose recent winning form makes him one of the more credible prominent challengers to Rockonliam.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to last the trip at Ballinrobe 36 days ago after being committed to the front too early. An inconsistent sort who is best caught fresh over 2½m on a sound surface; today's conditions are suitable but he needs to keep something in reserve.

races.paceDynamic: Rockonliam is the confirmed lone front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to press him from the outset, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m3½f trip on Good ground — a scenario that typically suits a horse of his make-up. Behind him, Ballyearl, Ned In The Park, Paul Collins, Clody Diamond, and Burru will look to occupy the prominent positions, but the field contains far more natural front-and-prominent types than can physically hold those spots: In The Trenches, Listentillitellyea, Sophia Rose, and Malbas are all true prominent racers who will be squeezed back into a midfield role against their preference. With a single pace-setter dictating an honest but uncontested rhythm on Good turf, the race sets up most naturally for horses who can travel prominently just off the leader and produce a clean jumping round — a seat close to the pace without the energy cost of fighting for it. The tactical verdict is clear: genuine prominent types who secure a natural position just behind Rockonliam are favoured, while hold-up horses face a stiff ask if the pace is moderate and the winning move is made before the last.

watchPoints.text: Burru won on Good ground 36 days ago and has a 15-run record on the surface showing consistent involvement — watch for him to sit prominently and mount a sustained challenge from the second-last.
Kashchei is the form horse in the hold-up group, winning over 21f on Good ground last time; if the pace slackens at any point, watch for him to produce an eye-catching late run from the rear.

Rockonliam will attempt to lead from flag to finish uncontested — watch his jumping closely, particularly at the first few fences, as any error at this stage could unsettle the entire pace structure of the race.

The cluster of redistributed prominent types (In The Trenches, Sophia Rose, Listentillitellyea, Malbas) will create early positional pressure behind Rockonliam — watch the first three furlongs for scrimmaging that could catch out horses with inexperienced or conditional riders.

Juke Hill and Juke Hill's trainer Gordon Elliott have a 2/10 14-day strike rate here — watch for Juke Hill to be produced with a well-timed late run if the race develops into a strongly-run affair that stretches the field.

races.name: Racing Again July 3rd Rated Novice Chase

runners_data.name: Lawful Ruler
runners_data.note: Decent Wexford form and runs prominently by nature but with so many speed-hungry rivals in this field he is likely squeezed out of his favoured pitch; 71 days off is a concern and the conditional pilot adds a layer of uncertainty at a novice chase level.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last of ten on our figures, he was well beaten in a hunter chase at Tramore latest, running out of his depth down in trip. Effective at 3m on good ground, but requires a higher level of opportunity to show his true ability.

runners_data.name: Chichester Park
runners_data.note: A.J. Martin's runner arrives on a 30-day break with respectable Good-ground form but has been redistributed to a hold-up position that flatters his map placement — he genuinely wants to race prominently and giving away his natural position in this traffic is a meaningful negative; Slevin is a strong booking but the horse needs his style to work.
runners_data.comment: Chase debut at Kilbeggan last month was encouraging — second beaten 11 lengths — and there should be more to offer over jumps. Effective between 2m and 2½m, he comes into this yet to score but has the profile of a horse still finding his feet.

runners_data.name: Costacurta
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's six-year-old has a consistent profile of placing on Good ground and races naturally in the prominent-to-midfield range, meaning he is well-suited to the position the race will actually give him — Darragh O'Keeffe is an ideal pilot for a horse that needs to be produced with precision.
runners_data.comment: Chase debut at Tramore last month was encouraging — third over a shorter trip than ideal — and he is expected to improve significantly now stepped up in distance. Acts on good ground over today's trip and has a trainer firing on all cylinders; the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Ephesus
runners_data.note: The only true hold-up horse in the field, which gives him a structurally distinct role, but his recent form reads 0460-7 and his Going record at similar trips is modest at 9 from 15; blinkers applied here suggest connections are trying to sharpen him but the raw form is a significant barrier.
runners_data.comment: Chase debut at Kilbeggan 15 days ago served as a tune-up rather than a form exercise, well beaten over this trip. First-time tongue-tie applied; he has the going in his favour but has been erratic across both disciplines.

runners_data.name: Garnacho
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's seven-year-old won over 2m on Good and ran second over this trip at the same conditions last time; Thomas O'Connor's claim is a minor worry but the horse's natural pace-prominent style fits the second tier behind Reiki Revolution, and his Good-ground jumping record is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Second at Listowel last month, beaten just 3 lengths in a handicap hurdle, showed he is in fine fettle for a new yard and more should be forthcoming over fences. Effective at 2½m on good ground, the first-time tongue-tie is new but the profile is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Howdoyalikeherhome
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner wears a hood and has a solid placed record on Good ground at extended trips; he is a natural prominent type who should find a clean berth just off the pace in a race where the true lead is already taken, making him a tactically well-placed runner without needing to fight for position.
runners_data.comment: Chase debut at Kilbeggan last month was an introductory run, fourth beaten 30 lengths without being put under pressure. A consistent hurdler with scope for improvement over fences at longer trips; first-time blinkers add an element of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Londonofficecallin
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's nine-year-old is a winner three times on similar conditions and genuinely wants to race up with the pace, but the sheer volume of prominent-style runners pushes him into the mapped midfield — racing against his instinct over 2m3½f on a 15-day turnaround is an energy cost the race shape will impose on him.
runners_data.comment: Encouraging chase debut at Kilbeggan 15 days ago — second beaten 3¼ lengths despite having ground to make up, looking like he wants a stiffer test. Useful across both disciplines, likely to have more to offer over longer trips, and today's stiff track looks ideal; first-time tongue-tie applied.

runners_data.name: Maxi Mac Gold
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's runner carries a tongue-tie and breast girth and has had a mixed campaign; a true prominent racer by nature, he is mapped to midfield because there is simply no room for him up front, and a pulled-up run in his recent form string adds concern that he lacks the consistency to overcome that tactical disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Back on better ground at Kilbeggan latest, fourth beaten 21 lengths in a beginners chase — a step forward for him over fences, though he has been inconsistent. First-time tongue-tie and blinkers off a short break; capable on his best day but not straightforward.

runners_data.name: Mister Pink
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's eight-year-old has a tidy placed record but every one of those placed runs came racing prominently on Good ground — being shuffled back into a midfield berth strips away his structural advantage, and while his consistency is admirable his ceiling appears moderate at this OR.
runners_data.comment: Never at the races at Punchestown 23 days ago, held without threatening in a handicap chase over today's trip. Acts on good ground and the assessment is he would do better over a longer distance in handicaps, so the case for him here is limited.

runners_data.name: Reiki Revolution
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's confirmed pace-setter won over 2m on Good and will lead from the front with Conor Stone-Walsh aboard; two unfinished runs from six starts add a jumping reliability question but on a day where the tempo is his to set, he becomes the pivotal race-shaper regardless of his own finishing probability.
runners_data.comment: Exit from a novice chase at Roscommon 22 days ago when already under pressure masks a horse who can do better over fences, particularly now the trip is increased. Typically held up for a late run, with first-time hood and tongue-tie; should be more competitive stepped up in distance.

races.paceDynamic: Reiki Revolution is the confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead aggressively, Conor Stone-Walsh can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over the 2m3½f trip on Good ground at Wexford. The field is heavily stacked with prominent-style horses — Maxi Mac Gold, Londonofficecallin, Mister Pink, Lawful Ruler and Garnacho all want to race forward but cannot all occupy that territory, meaning several will be forced to settle closer to midfield than their natural instinct dictates. Costacurta, Howdoyalikeherhome and Chichester Park are the true midfield-to-prominent types best placed to track the pace without fighting their rider, while Ephesus is the sole genuine hold-up operator. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can track Reiki Revolution at a comfortable clip without burning energy fighting for position — horses racing close to the pace in a rhythm-controlled, moderate-tempo chase have the clearest path to victory. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate; Reiki Revolution is almost certain to secure the lead unchallenged, with Costacurta and Howdoyalikeherhome best positioned to naturally hold the next seats.

watchPoints.text: Reiki Revolution's two Unseated Rider runs in recent form — if he makes a jumping error at a critical fence, the whole pace dynamic collapses and horses further back are immediately back in contention.

The cluster of prominent horses (Maxi Mac Gold, Londonofficecallin, Mister Pink, Lawful Ruler) all wanting forward positions creates a risk of early jostling and a faster-than-expected early gallop, which could compress the field and bring hold-up types like Ephesus back into play later.

Chichester Park's redistribution to a hold-up role for J.J. Slevin is worth monitoring — if Slevin ignores the map and pushes forward as his natural instinct would suggest, it could disrupt the second tier of prominent horses tracking Reiki Revolution.

Costacurta's trainer Henry De Bromhead has a 1/15 strike rate in the 14-day window, but the 32-day gap here and consistent placed record on this going suggests the horse is produced fresh rather than frequently — note how fluently he jumps in the early stages as a key indicator.

Good ground is confirmed throughout the card at Wexford and has remained consistent all day — no deterioration risk, meaning form on this surface is a reliable reference point and pace advantage is unlikely to be distorted by ground variation late in the race.
